description: Sets a timeout interval in seconds after which, if no data has been received from the server, ssh will send a keepalive message.
Sets the number of server-alive messages which may be sent without ssh receiving any messages back from the server. If this threshold is reached, ssh will disconnect from the server.
Controls whether ssh automatically adds new host keys. Options: yes, no, accept-new, off, ask.
Specifies a file to use for the user host key database instead of the default ~/.ssh/known_hosts.
Specifies whether to use compression. Values: yes or no.
Specifies the compression level to use (1–9, where 1 is fast and 9 is best). Only applies when Compression=yes.
Specifies whether X11 connections will be automatically redirected over the secure channel and DISPLAY set. Values: yes or no.
Specifies whether ssh should terminate the connection if it cannot set up all requested dynamic, tunnel, local, and remote port forwardings.
Specifies the timeout (in seconds) used when connecting to the SSH server.
Specifies that ssh should only use the configured authentication identity and certificate files, even if ssh-agent or a PKCS11Provider offers more identities.
Specifies whether keys should be automatically added to a running ssh-agent. Values: yes, no, ask, confirm.
(macOS only) Specifies whether the system keychain should be used to store passphrases. Values: yes or no.
Specifies whether the system should send TCP keepalive messages to the other side. Values: yes or no.
Gives the verbosity level used when logging messages. Values: QUIET, FATAL, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, DEBUG1, DEBUG2, DEBUG3.
Specifies the ciphers allowed for protocol version 2 in order of preference.
Specifies the MAC (message authentication code) algorithms in order of preference.
Specifies the available KEX (Key Exchange) algorithms.
Specifies the host key signature algorithms that the client wants to use in order of preference.
If set to yes, passphrase/password querying will be disabled. Useful in scripts and other batch jobs.
Enables sharing of multiple sessions over a single network connection. Values: yes, no, ask, auto, autoask.
Specify the path to the control socket used for connection sharing.
When used in conjunction with ControlMaster, specifies that the master connection should remain open in the background after the initial client connection has been closed.
Specifies which environment variables to send to the server. Variables are space-separated and may include wildcards.
Directly specify one or more environment variables and their contents to be sent to the server.
Specifies whether to request a pseudo-tty for the session. Values: no, yes, force, auto.
Specifies a command to execute on the remote machine after connecting.
